component.name: Claude Crab
component.summary: Watch Claude Code work from the corner of your eye

description.p: Claude Crab puts a small pixel character in a strip just above your panel and animates it to match what Claude Code is doing, so you can tell at a glance without switching windows.

At rest it sleeps in a corner. When a session starts working it walks, and the gait changes with the tool in use. When Claude is waiting on you it stops, turns to face you, and waves — the one state where you are the thing holding work up.
It reads Claude Code hook events and nothing else. It never inspects your prompts, code, or transcripts, and it makes no network connections.

ul.li: Click-through overlay that never steals focus or covers your panel
A single character reflecting every running session at once
Distinct animations for waiting on input, finishing, and failing
An optional variant with a top hat and monocle
Runs as a systemd user service

description.p: Pinning now remembers the crab's height across restarts, and the release Flatpak bundle builds again.

Complete rewrite in Rust: no Qt dependency, a wlr-layer-shell backend on Wayland and a floating-window backend for macOS and Windows. The crab can be dragged to any point on the screen and pinned against dragging from the right-click menu.
Documents installing the hooks from inside the Flatpak, and fixes the hook installer silently reporting no hooks when it cannot read the configuration directory at all.
Adds a party hat variant, and fixes the event inbox growing without bound while the crab was not running.
